summary: Switches a view or a filter of the same content, shown side by side as attached segments: List, Grid or Board, the token type filter, light or dark, the brand of a preview. The choice applies at once, on the current screen. The selected segment is a raised plate on the track.
whenToUse: Switching a view or a filter of the same content: List, Grid or Board; the token type filter (All, Color, Spacing); Light or Dark; Side by side or Overlay in a compare; an expression picker.

Short options where seeing every option at once helps the choice: two to five usually, more for filters people switch between often (status filters). On a phone the track scrolls sideways and never widens the page.

Switching between sibling pages or spaces that are separate addresses (Library and Studio, Overview and Activity): give every segment an href. Each segment is a link, the current one marked as the page you are on.
Appearance default everywhere: the selected segment is a raised plate (the raised surface, a hairline edge, the raised elevation) with ink text.
Appearance strong only for the global space switch (Library and Studio in the top bar): the current segment fills with Deep Harbor. One on the site; never for a filter or a view switch.
The change applies immediately, with no Save button.
Size sm in dense toolbars, menus and panels; md everywhere else, including a page's filter bar, where it matches the md search field and Select beside it. Heights follow the density setting.
fullWidth inside a narrow panel or menu, so the segments share the width equally.
whenNotToUse: Switching between sections or panels of different content (Settings groups, a component page's Usage and Code): use Tabs (underline), which link each tab to its panel.
A tab-like row built with your own CSS: never. A view switch is this control, a section switch is Tabs, nothing in between.
A setting in a form that is saved later: use RadioGroup, which shows a label and help per option.
Long labels, or options people pick once and forget: use Select.
Turning one thing on or off: use Switch.
Triggering actions (Export, Delete): use Button or an attached ButtonGroup.

dos.title: Short, parallel labels
dos.text: One or two words per segment, same grammatical form, so the set reads as one choice.

dos.title: Label outside the track
dos.text: Put a visible label to the left of the track, as a caption on its center line, and name the group with it (aria-labelledby, or the same words in label). The track holds the options and nothing else.

dos.title: Filters keep the default plate
dos.text: A list filtered by status: the selected filter is the raised plate, like every other segmented control. Six short filters are fine; on a phone they scroll sideways. Strong is kept for the space switch.

dos.title: Always start with a selection
dos.text: A segmented control shows the current mode. Pass value or defaultValue so one segment is always selected.

dos.title: Counts sit in a count tag
dos.text: Give a filter its count with the item's count field, never inside the label: it renders as a small neutral tag after the label and looks the same in every segment, selected or not: only the label's ink follows the selection.

donts.title: Actions dressed as segments
donts.text: Segments select a mode; they never run a command. "Export" and "Share" belong on buttons.

donts.title: The label inside the track
donts.text: Never put the group's label in the same pill as the options. Inside one container it reads as one more option ("Brand" next to "Bridge" and "Ocean"). Keep it outside, to the left.

donts.title: Too many or too long options
donts.text: Two or three words per segment make the track longer than the screen and stop reading as one control. Keep labels to one or two words, or use Select.

accessibility: Base UI RadioGroup with native button radios: role radiogroup on the row, role radio and aria-checked on each segment.

With href on the segments it is navigation, not a choice: a nav named by label, each segment a link, the current one aria-current="page". Tab moves from link to link; there is no arrow-key selection and no checked state.
Tab enters the group on the selected segment and leaves it; arrow keys move the selection, Home and End jump to the ends.
Give the group a name: aria-labelledby pointing at the visible label outside the track, or label (aria-label) when the context already names it.

The selected segment is marked by a raised plate with a neutral hairline edge and the raised elevation (or the Deep Harbor fill with strong) and ink text, not by color alone. Never a Deep Harbor or focus-colored outline: that reads as keyboard focus.
When the track scrolls, arrow keys still move the selection and the selected segment scrolls into view.
The focus ring (focus.ring.color) shows on keyboard focus only (:focus-visible), inside the segment a step off its edge; a click draws no ring.
Rendered without JavaScript, the HTML keeps role, aria-checked and data-value, so a small script can drive it: flip aria-checked and tabindex, and handle arrow keys.
contentGuidelines: Sentence case nouns or adjectives: "Compact", "Dark", "Grid". No verbs: segments are states, not actions.
One or two words. Drop the shared word: "Light, Dark", not "Light theme, Dark theme".
Name the group with what is being chosen: "Density", "Brand", "Themes shown". When it changes only a preview, say so: "Preview brand".
A visible label is a caption to the left of the track (caption size, muted text color), never a segment inside it.

anatomy.strong: Strong appearance: Deep Harbor selected segment, only for the global space switch
anatomy.leading: Decoration before the label, for example a color swatch
anatomy.label: Label
anatomy.links: Navigation mode: segments are links, the current one is the page you are on (the same plate as a selected segment; strong only on the space switch)
